spec_match.rationale: Uses getPathData({normalize:true}) for exactly what the explainer says normalization is for — reducing both endpoints to interpolable absolute cubics — and writes every frame with a real setPathData call.

interactive.rationale: The t slider writes real frames (d attribute measured changing: 333 chars at t=0, 367 at t=0.6), and play/stop run and halt a requestAnimationFrame ping-pong loop with the stop state honestly reported.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Card frames morphing as the crbug use case and promises normalize + interpolate + setPathData; the page does precisely that.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles mismatched segment counts (11 vs 6, padded with degenerate cubics), L-to-C promotion, Z closure, unsupported builds (play disabled, no fake frames), and stop-at-current-t cancellation without jumping to a terminal state.

references.rationale: chromestatus, spec normalize anchor, and the crbug the lede cites are all linked.

conformance.rationale: normalize-emits-only-absolute-mlcz and setpathdata-roundtrip assertions pin the two primitives the morph is built from.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 153 via Playwright CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable): flagged runs show the green normalization verdict (star 11 / blob 6 / matched 11), a visibly intermediate star-blob shape on screenshots at t=0.31 and t=0.6, play/stop verified; unflagged runs show the red honest fallback with endpoints still drawn; console and network clean everywhere.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts normalized/matched counts on supported builds and the explicit fallback assert on unsupported ones.

design_system.rationale: All colours from variables; disabled buttons keep the global bg+color pair at reduced opacity (AA on ivory held).

accessibility.rationale: Slider labelled with live t value, morph SVG has role=img with a label, figures caption the endpoints, output is aria-live, play/stop are native buttons with disabled state.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Endpoint figures stack under 640px; no horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3; controls wrap with 44px targets.

openQuestions.title: Subdivide instead of padding when matching segment counts
openQuestions.detail: Padding the shorter endpoint with degenerate point-cubics is correct but collapses part of the morph's motion into one corner near t=1. Splitting the blob's longest cubics (de Casteljau at t=0.5) until counts match would distribute motion evenly and is a nicer teaching artifact for the same API surface.

guidanceConsulted.query: range slider input accessible labeling and keyboard
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Native range input with text value mirror.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: t slider is native, arrow-key operable, with the numeric t echoed in its label and output.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible status updates live region after button action
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Expose animation state through text and control disabled states.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Play disables itself while running, stop re-enables it, and the aria-live output names the exact t where the loop halted.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Grid columns that collapse at narrow widths.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The two endpoint figures are a 2-column grid collapsing to 1 under 640px; verified at 360px.

summary: Built and verified 2026-10-25 in the weekly hardening coverage sweep. Flagged Chromium 153 runs the real morph: both endpoints normalized to cubics via getPathData({normalize:true}), counts matched 11/11, every frame a setPathData write, play/stop exercised with the frame-on-screen-equals-last-write invariant stated in the output. Unflagged runs prove the no-simulation fallback. Clean console/network and read screenshots at both viewport classes in both modes.
